title: Jensen Huang is re-hired by Nvidia
gist: Repost of a CNBC report that Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO effective immediately, citing input from senior U.S. government levels that his return poses no national security risk; shares jumped more than 26% (linked headline says 27%).

insights.claim: Nvidia announced on a Monday that Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO effective immediately, sending its shares up more than 26%.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Shows how much of Nvidia's valuation the market attributes to Huang personally.
insights.quote: sending shares of the chipmaker soaring more than 26%
insights.locator: Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang

insights.claim: Nvidia's board said it unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with him.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Board reversal ends key-person uncertainty but raises governance-independence questions.
insights.locator: The board of directors said it

insights.claim: Nvidia's board said it received input from senior levels of the United States government and is confident Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Washington's involvement in a CEO decision underscores Nvidia's status as a strategic national asset.
insights.quote: received input from senior levels of the United States government
insights.locator: The board of directors said it

insights.claim: Huang framed his return as leading one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Signals strategic continuity of Nvidia's AI-infrastructure narrative.
insights.quote: lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution
